metais help schemas — Writing schemas: every keyword and format, and rules
across rows.

Example:

A table whose rows each answer one criterion, from the specification's chapter
13. uniqueKeys refuses a second row for one criterion, and coverage reports each
Level A or AA criterion no row answers; a row for 1.2.6, a Level AAA criterion,
is allowed and not required.

  {
    "type": "array",
    "uniqueKeys": ["/criterion"],
    "coverage": {
      "key": "/criterion",
      "values": ["1.1.1", "1.2.1", "1.2.2", "1.2.3", "1.2.4", "1.2.5"]
    },
    "items": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["criterion", "conformance"],
      "properties": {
        "criterion": {
          "type": "string",
          "enum": [
            "1.1.1", "1.2.1", "1.2.2", "1.2.3", "1.2.4", "1.2.5", "1.2.6"
          ]
        },
        "conformance": {
          "enum": [
            "Supports", "Partially Supports", "Does Not Support",
            "Not Applicable", "Not Evaluated"
          ]
        }
      }
    }
  }

metais schema <package> <input> --fields lists its two rules in words, directly
beneath the array's line:

  rows must include, at `/criterion`, each of: "1.1.1", "1.2.1", …
  no two rows share `/criterion`

The dialect:
Every .json, .yaml and .yml file under inputs/ is a schema of JSON Schema
2020-12, compiled when the package is opened whether or not an input names it.
$schema, where a schema gives it, is
https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema; any other, and $vocabulary, is
refused. A schema uses only these keywords:

Asserted:
  Core         $schema $id $ref $defs $anchor $dynamicRef $dynamicAnchor
               $comment
  Applicator   allOf anyOf oneOf not if then else dependentSchemas properties
               patternProperties additionalProperties propertyNames prefixItems
               items contains
  Unevaluated  unevaluatedProperties unevaluatedItems
  Validation   type enum const multipleOf minimum exclusiveMinimum maximum
               exclusiveMaximum minLength maxLength pattern minItems maxItems
               uniqueItems minContains maxContains minProperties maxProperties
               required dependentRequired
  Rows         uniqueKeys coverage
  Format       format
Annotations, never asserted:
  Meta-data    title description default deprecated readOnly writeOnly examples
  Content      contentEncoding contentMediaType contentSchema

default fills a value nobody supplied (metais help inputs). Any other keyword is
refused as schema.keyword_unknown, so a misspelt requried or maxLenght is found,
not ignored. The one exception is a keyword beginning x-: it is the author's own
annotation, carried unchanged and never interpreted, so it may hold a note but
never a rule.

A $ref resolves only inside the package: to a schema file under inputs/ by its
path from the referring file, or by its root's $id when it has one, and then
only by that $id; to an anchor or a JSON Pointer within one; or to a 2020-12
meta-schema. Nothing is ever fetched.

pattern and the names of patternProperties are ECMA-262 regular expressions,
unanchored: write ^ and $ to match a whole string. A lookahead, a lookbehind, a
backreference and a repeat bound above 1000 are refused.

Formats:
format names one of these, and is asserted: a string that is not of its format
is a finding, and a value that is not a string passes.

  date-time              An RFC 3339 date and time, with its offset:
                         2026-10-23T09:30:00Z
  date                   An RFC 3339 full date: 2026-10-23
  time                   An RFC 3339 time, with its offset: 09:30:00+02:00
  duration               An RFC 3339 duration (Appendix A): P1DT12H
  email                  An RFC 5321 mailbox: ada@example.org
  hostname               An RFC 1123 host name: docs.example.org
  ipv4                   An IPv4 address in dotted-decimal form: 192.0.2.1
  ipv6                   An RFC 4291 IPv6 address: 2001:db8::1
  uri                    An absolute RFC 3986 URI: https://example.org/a?b=c
  uri-reference          An RFC 3986 URI or relative reference: ../a#b
  uuid                   An RFC 4122 UUID in its string form:
                         f81d4fae-7dec-11d0-a765-00a0c91e6bf6
  uri-template           An RFC 6570 URI template: https://example.org/{id}
  json-pointer           An RFC 6901 JSON Pointer: /rows/0/name
  relative-json-pointer  A relative JSON Pointer: 1/name

Any other format, idn-email, idn-hostname, iri, iri-reference and regex among
them, is refused as schema.format_unsupported: write a pattern instead, or say
what you expect in the input's meaning document.

Rules across the rows of a table:
JSON Schema judges each row of a table alone. Two keywords of this
specification, written in the schema of the array, state a rule across its rows:

  uniqueKeys  The columns that identify a row, as 1 to 8 JSON Pointers into one
              row. A later row with the same values in all of them is refused,
              at that row. Several pointers make one key together: ["/standard",
              "/clause"] allows one clause in two standards.
  coverage    An object of key, one such pointer, and values, the values that
              column must hold. Each value no row holds is reported. List what
              is required, not everything that may appear.

Values are compared as JSON values, so 1.0 equals 1. A row with no value in a
key column takes no part in either rule, so make the column required when every
row needs one. A rule between the fields of one row needs neither keyword: write
if and then in the item schema. A rule between inputs belongs in the input
constraints (input_constraints in metais help manifest).

Both keywords are this specification's, so a JSON Schema tool that knows only
2020-12 ignores them: say each rule in the input's meaning document too, so that
a supplier gathers complete data before validating it. metais check refuses a
coverage value the item schema refuses, or more values than maxItems allows, as
schema.unsatisfiable, and warns of a key pointer no row declares, as
schema.key_not_declared.

metais check [<dir>] reports every finding of every schema at once. metais
schema <package> <input> --fields lists an input's fields and rules, one line
each. The specification's chapter 5 states the dialect, and chapter 13 how to
write a package's schemas.
